newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan shilling rises on coffee pre-finance.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan shilling rises on coffee pre-finance.

text.p: The Ugandan shilling rose by around 1.1 percent in February, reversing losses in January.

The central Bank of Uganda (BOU) economic and financial indicators for February showed that the monthly interbank mid-rate gained to 1033.11 shillings per dollar in February compared to 1044.85 shillings per dollar in January 1997.
The shilling gains were largely attributed to increased coffee pre-finance and other inflows, which also pushed up the volume of transactions in the interbank forex market.
Gross foreign exchange purchases rose to $129.79 million in February from $120.26 million in January while gross sales rose to $123.03 million from $116.31 million in the same period.

The reserves held by commercial banks rose by 10.39 billion from 53.63 billion as at end-January to 64.02 billion as at end- February. The currency issued gained by 1.02 billion from 249.88 at end-January to 250.90 billion at end-February.
Money supply (M2) grew by 1.6 percent from 644.9 billion shillings at end-November to 655.4 billion shillings as at end-December, an annual growth rate of 17.7 percent.
A similar growth rate was recorded during the fiscal year 1995/96 and depicted a steady trend in money supply.

The indicators showed that currency in circulation rose by 2.3 percent in February from January to 22.1 billion shillings while private demand deposits increased by 2.6 percent to 229.7 billion shillings in the same period. Private savings deposits remained stable at 205 billion shillings.
The central bank blamed the overall growth in M2 on slight increases in the foreign assets of the banking system and private sector credit.
The bank gave no predictions for the month of March.
